name: Easy Pressure Cooker Crab Risotto with Asparagus, Parmesan & Parsley

instructions.primary_message: Set a 6-quart electric pressure cooker to sauté on HIGH.
While the pressure cooker heats up, peel and small dice shallots.
Once the pressure cooker insert is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add shallot, garlic, salt, and pepper; cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 2 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
2 tsp minced garlic
½ tsp salt
¼ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water. Add rice to the insert and continue to cook, stirring frequently, until starting to turn golden, 3-4 minutes more.

Add broth, then stir to combine. Lock lid and set to pressure cook on HIGH for 6 minutes. When the rice is done, allow pressure to release naturally for 10 minutes, then drape a clean towel over the vent and manually release any remaining pressure. Remove lid.
Meanwhile, wash, dry, and shave parsley leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Place in a small bowl and set aside.
Wash, dry, and snap (or cut) off woody ends of the asparagus; cut spears into 2-inch long pieces.

When the rice is done, add asparagus, crab (breaking the meat into bite-sized pieces if necessary), Parmesan, cream, and water to the pressure cooker, then stir to combine.  Set the pressure cooker to sauté on HIGH. Cook, stirring constantly, until asparagus is tender, cheese is melted, and risotto is warmed through, 5-6 minutes. (Add more water, a few tablespoons at a time, if needed, to keep the rice from sticking to the bottom.)
instructions.secondary_message:
2 (227 g) pkg surimi (imitation crab meat)
1 cup Parmesan cheese, shredded
½ cup heavy whipping cream

instructions.primary_message: To serve, divide risotto between bowls. Top with parsley and enjoy!
